name: Spliceosome-Mediated RNA Trans-splicing (SMaRT)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Replace the mutant portion of a pre-mRNA with a corrected RNA sequence through spliceosome-mediated trans-splicing, restoring a functional transcript and protein.
molecularDefect: Mutations affecting coding regions where replacement of part of the transcript is preferable to transcript degradation or exon skipping.
diseaseMechanism: An engineered RNA trans-splicing molecule binds the target pre-mRNA through a binding domain and recruits the endogenous spliceosome to perform trans-splicing, replacing the mutant RNA segment with a therapeutic sequence.
suitableVariantTypes: Coding-region mutations; nonsense mutations; frameshift mutations; selected missense mutations; multi-exon pathogenic regions.
typicalDiseases: Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR); Hemophilia A (F8); Epidermolysis Bullosa (COL7A1); Retinitis Pigmentosa (experimental); Huntington disease (experimental).
rnaTargetRegion: Intronic sequences adjacent to the intended trans-splicing site within the target pre-mRNA.
transcriptRequirement: Active transcription of the target gene to provide endogenous pre-mRNA substrate.
designRules: Identify an efficient intronic binding site; optimize splice donor/acceptor elements; minimize competition with endogenous cis-splicing; validate repaired transcript by RT-PCR and sequencing.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible pre-mRNA binding regions are preferred to facilitate RTM hybridization.
offTargetConsiderations: Off-target trans-splicing; formation of aberrant chimeric transcripts; unintended splice junctions.
advantages: Can replace large mutant transcript regions; potentially mutation-independent within the replaced segment; preserves endogenous gene regulation.
limitations: Low trans-splicing efficiency; competition with endogenous cis-splicing; challenging delivery; no approved therapies.
